passage:
Dear Tarun,

I'm writing because I find it easier to say this without watching your face. You told me about the affair three weeks ago. Since then I've been angry every morning and hopeful every night, and I don't know which one is telling the truth. You say you want to rebuild, and part of me wants that too.

So here is what I need. Full honesty, including the answers I don't like. Time, without being asked how I'm doing every day. And your patience if I go cold.

I also want you to know that I might decide our marriage can't be saved. If I do, it won't mean I didn't love you or that I gave up too easily.

I'll give you my answer when I have one.

Nilesh

qa.q: How long ago did Tarun tell Nilesh about the affair?
What two feelings does Nilesh describe, and how does Nilesh feel about them?
qa.a: Anger every morning and hope every night. Nilesh does not know which one is telling the truth.

qa.q: What conditions does Nilesh set, and why are they reasonable?
qa.a: Full honesty, time without daily check-ins, and patience with coldness. They give Nilesh a way to judge whether trust can grow again without rushing.

qa.q: How might Tarun react on reading that Nilesh may decide the marriage cannot be saved?
qa.a: Tarun may feel afraid or sad, but the letter also says that choice would not mean Nilesh didn't love Tarun, which may make it easier to hear.

grounding: Shows a partner's hope tangled with anger after an affair, setting conditions of honesty and time, and stating that ending the marriage is a possible, legitimate choice.

passage:
Dear Usha,

You asked what I've decided. I haven't. Here's where I am.

It's been three months since I found out about Farhan's affair. He ended it the day I found out. He cries, he says he'll do anything, he wants us to rebuild. Some mornings I look at him making my tea and feel hope, almost like before. By evening I'm so angry I can't stay in the same room.

I've told him my conditions if we try: full honesty, any question answered, no deleting messages, and counselling together every week. And time, as much as I need, with no "aren't you over it yet".

He agreed to all of it.

But I've also told him, and myself, that I'm free to decide this marriage can't be saved. Staying wouldn't make me weak. Leaving wouldn't either.

I'll write again after the next session.

Ayesha

qa.q: How long has it been since Ayesha found out about the affair?
What is Ayesha feeling about Farhan's wish to rebuild?
qa.a: Ayesha feels hope tangled with anger, hopeful some mornings and so angry by evening she can't stay in the same room.

qa.q: What conditions has Ayesha set, and why do they matter?
qa.a: Full honesty, answered questions, no deleting messages, weekly counselling and time; they make rebuilding safer while keeping Ayesha free to leave.

qa.q: How might Farhan feel about Ayesha's conditions?
qa.a: Farhan seems desperate to rebuild and willing to accept them, though he may fear she will still decide to leave.

grounding: The letter shows a young spouse whose partner wants to rebuild after an affair, setting conditions like honesty and time while staying free to leave.

passage:
Samir, you asked me straight, so I'll answer straight. It's Lakshmi. Yes, I'm still with Hemant. Six months after I found out about the affair.

People think staying means I'm weak. My own sister said so. Others think I should forgive and move on because he's sorry. Neither of them lives in my body.

Some days I look at him and I remember why I married him. Other days I want to throw his phone into the lake. Both feelings are real. Hope and anger, all tangled up.

What's helped is conditions. I told him: you answer every question, however many times I ask. You don't rush me. We go to counselling every Thursday. He's kept all of it so far.

And I've told him plainly that I might still leave. That door is open. If I walk through it someday, it won't be weakness either. It'll just be my decision.

qa.q: On which day do Lakshmi and Hemant go to counselling?
What is Lakshmi feeling about staying with Hemant?
qa.a: Lakshmi feels hope and anger tangled together, sometimes remembering why they married and sometimes furious.

qa.q: How is Lakshmi making rebuilding possible without giving up her choice?
qa.a: Lakshmi has set conditions, honest answers, no rushing and weekly counselling, while keeping the freedom to leave.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi's sister see her choice to stay?
qa.a: Lakshmi's sister sees it as weakness, not understanding what Lakshmi is actually feeling and deciding.

grounding: The monologue shows a young spouse whose partner wants to rebuild after an affair, setting conditions and time while staying free to decide the marriage can't be saved.
